key_insight: Under post-acoustic approximation, the piston effect in supercritical fluids reduces to a diffusion problem with a spatially uniform pressure source, enabling exact analytical solutions for the thermal response.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a fast, closed-form way to predict heat transfer and bulk pressurization in near-critical systems without resolving acoustic waves or running full simulations.
method: Derive exact 1D analytical solutions in Cartesian and spherical geometries.
Treat pressure as spatially uniform and time-dependent, linked directly to boundary heat flux.
Introduce an effective boundary condition that accounts for container heat capacity and wall temperature evolution.
evidence_signal: The analytical model is compared with Spacelab D-2 experiment data and is reported to match well without numerical simulation.
watch_item: The approach relies on a linear, post-acoustic approximation, so accuracy may degrade when acoustic dynamics or strong nonlinear effects become important.
paper_title: Exact analytical solutions for the piston effect in supercritical fluids under post-acoustic approximation -- Short-time asymptotics, thermal penetration depth and comparison with the Spacelab D-2 experiments
